messages:
sara: heads up — staging dashboards showed increased p95 this morning. traced to query layer doing authz per-child-fanout. not a full outage but noticeable tail.

alex: can you paste the trace sample? is it the per-panel authz call we discussed in the last rfc?

sara: sample trace: 
```
[2026-02-03T07:03:21Z] root=dashboard:id=xyz fanout=12 panel=metrics shard=3 authz=rpc permissions-svc took=260ms
[2026-02-03T07:03:21Z] root=dashboard:id=xyz fetch panel=metrics took=14ms
[2026-02-03T07:03:21Z] root=dashboard:id=xyz fanout=12 panel=alerts authz=rpc permissions-svc took=480ms
```
Essentially each child node does a permissions RPC. Under concurrent requests this multiplies latency.

ben: yep. load test reproduced this: heavy fanout + slow permissions store -> p95 jumps. Two high-level mitigations: (1) move authz earlier by computing required perms once and (2) cache permission results scoped to request or short TTL.

maya: both have tradeoffs. early compute needs accurate query->perm mapping; caching needs careful invalidation if permissions change mid-request.

alex: proposal: request-scoped cache keyed by (user-epoch). idea: on request start, fetch a lightweight user-epoch token (cheap check, usually in the auth cookie), then cache perms for the lifetime of the request keyed to that epoch. If epoch changes (role revoke), new requests pick new epoch. avoids long-lived global cache.

jamie: thoughts on acquiring epoch cheaply? we shouldn't call perms-svc on every request to get epoch. maybe the authn token includes an epoch claim that rotates on policy update. fallback to a single perms call if missing.

ben: also need to bound memory: many concurrent dashboard requests could amplify memory usage. implement a bounded LRU per-worker with per-request lightweight map + global shard-local cache with size cap and eviction metrics. add telemetry: cache_size, evictions, hit_rate per minute.

sara: another angle: static analysis of query graph to compute the minimal set of required permissions up-front. run that analyzer as pipeline stage before fanout so we call authz once for the deduped permission set, then filter the fanout list. lowers RPC count.

maya: how do we handle dynamic query shapes (templated panels, runtime expansions)? analyzer must emit conservative superset of permissions; worst-case could hurt but usually still better than N RPCs. we should start with common panel types and expand.

alex: implementation sketch: pipeline A: query->perm analyzer emits permission keys; B: permission fetch with request-scoped cache; C: prune fanout nodes; D: execute fetches. feature-flag everything.

ben: quick perf estimates from microbench: dedupe-only reduced authz RPCs by ~70% in our synthetic dashboard, p95 improved ~35%. adding request-scoped cache with 30s TTL pushed p95 gain to ~60% in scenarios with repeated identical checks.

jamie: we also discussed pushing ACL deltas for Dedicated/Private customers to their query edge nodes. that would make authz local and eliminate RTTs but increases complexity: memory, sync correctness, operational burden. consider it as premium opt-in.

sara: action items: (1) spike request-scoped authz cache in console-query (alex + ben) with `authz.request_cache_ttl_ms` default 30000 and telemetry. (2) add simple query->perm analyzer for top-5 panel types (sara + jamie). (3) load test scenario that simulates many small panels fanout (ben). target: staging canary in 2w.

alex: I'll open a draft PR with the cache shim and local metrics: `console.query.authz_cache.hits` and `...misses`. will gate via `feature.authz_request_cache` flag.

maya: include correctness tests for revokes: simulate token epoch rotation mid-test and ensure no stale access. if cache shows >10% incorrect under harness, block rollout.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: staging rolling deploy scheduled 2026-02-05T02:00:00Z. integration tests and e2e will run.

ben: I'll attach the load scenario and test plan to the PR. also will include memory smoke test for per-worker cache under 10k concurrent requests.

sara: great. one more ops point: add alerting for cache hit_rate drop and authz RPC latency increase so we can fast-fail the rollout.

alex: will do. posting links and PR once ready. :rocket:
